edges.description: Insufficient nucleating capacity compromises spindle assembly, producing abnormal nuclear shape and aneuploidy.
Impaired progenitor division reduces cell output in both the developing brain and the developing eye.
The functional consequence of the retinal phenotype.

nodes.description: The cellular consequence, and the one that separates this disorder from the migration tubulinopathies. Patient fibroblasts show abnormal nuclear shape and aneuploidy - a division phenotype, not a motility phenotype. In a developing brain and retina, cells that divide unfaithfully produce fewer and abnormal progeny, which is the route to both microcephaly and the photoreceptor phenotype.

nodes.description: The tissue-level endpoint, affecting two organs that share a dependence on faithful progenitor division during development. Zebrafish morphants show reduced head volume and eye developmental anomalies with chorioretinal dysplasia, reproducing the human combination. The eye involvement is specifically photoreceptor-weighted, which is what makes it chorioretinopathy rather than a nonspecific ocular anomaly.

nodes.description: Biallelic TUBGCP4 variants - a recurrent synonymous variant that induces exon skipping, plus frameshift variants and a deletion - reduce the level of the gamma-tubulin ring complex. TUBGCP4 is a structural component of that complex, which regulates the nucleation and organization of microtubules. The lesion is therefore quantitative and upstream of polymer assembly: with less nucleating machinery, microtubule arrays are built incorrectly rather than built from faulty subunits.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic loss-of-function alleles. The allele classes themselves make the mechanism unambiguous - frameshifts, a deletion, and a synonymous variant shown to induce exon skipping are all loss-of-function, and the measured consequence is reduced gamma-TuRC level. This is the clearest LOSS_OF_FUNCTION assignment in the tubulin family, and contrasts with the dominant missense mechanisms of the tubulin isotype genes.
